original_title: Here's a first for Call of Duty: The Modern Warfare 4 beta will have a campaign mission and Warzone stuff
summary_en: Infinity Ward is shaking up the Call of Duty beta tradition by including a playable campaign mission and Warzone content for the first time. Players will get a taste of the single-player narrative alongside the familiar multiplayer offerings.

en.title: Modern Warfare 4 Beta Drops Campaign Mission and Warzone for First Time
en.summary: Infinity Ward is shaking up the Call of Duty beta tradition by including a playable campaign mission and Warzone content for the first time. Players will get a taste of the single-player narrative alongside the familiar multiplayer offerings.
en.body:
Call of Duty betas have long been a staple of the franchise, offering players a sneak peek at multiplayer action before launch. However, **Modern Warfare 4** is set to break the mold with a beta that includes unprecedented content: a playable campaign mission and a taste of **Warzone**. This marks a first for the series, aiming to provide a more holistic experience to fans.

The beta, kicking off on August 21st for pre-orders and later opening to all on August 28th, will feature the campaign mission "Entrenched." This mission plunges players into the heart of a conflict in North Korea, following a squad of South Korean marines and an embedded American on an offensive. Expect classic Call of Duty set pieces, from trench warfare to intense firefights, offering a glimpse into the narrative Infinity Ward has crafted. This inclusion suggests a strong confidence in the campaign's quality and a desire to showcase it alongside the multiplayer.

> "Entrenched" is the campaign mission that'll be playable early.

Beyond the campaign, the beta will also offer a look at **Warzone**. While not available during the initial pre-order access, the second weekend will see the new Zodiac Resurgence map playable. This integration promises to reveal how **Modern Warfare 4**'s gameplay innovations will translate into the battle royale experience, a crucial element for many players.

## A New Approach to Beta Testing

This ambitious beta structure isn't just about offering more content; it's about evolving how **Call of Duty** engages with its community. By providing access to a campaign mission and **Warzone**, Infinity Ward is not only testing core gameplay mechanics but also gauging player reception to narrative elements and the broader ecosystem. This move could set a new precedent for future **Call of Duty** releases, prioritizing a more comprehensive pre-launch experience. The developers have been focusing on refinements, addressing player feedback on aspects like muzzle flash, hipfire, and movement to enhance immersion without alienating dedicated players. The beta serves as the ultimate proving ground for these adjustments.

## What This Means for Fans

For players, this expanded beta means a deeper dive into what **Modern Warfare 4** truly offers. It’s an opportunity to not only test the multiplayer maps and modes like Kill Block, Rooftop, Silk Worm, Transit 213, Cachet, and Lotus, but also to experience the polished gunplay and narrative direction of the campaign. The inclusion of **Warzone** content further sweetens the deal, allowing fans to see how the latest **Modern Warfare** iteration impacts the popular free-to-play mode. This comprehensive preview allows for more informed decisions and builds significant anticipation for the full release.

## What's Next

The **Modern Warfare 4** beta runs from August 21st to 25th for pre-orders, with an open beta from August 28th to September 1st. The full game is slated for a global release on October 23rd, 2026, across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.

content_raw: Few things in gaming are more routine than a Call of Duty multiplayer beta, but this year's is actually a bit different. The Modern Warfare 4 beta kicking off on August 21 (for pre-orders only) will include the usual smattering of multiplayer modes, and in a series first, it'll also include a chunk of the campaign. "Entrenched" is the campaign mission that'll be playable early, and Infinity Ward has published a brief teaser for it (watch above). Based on what we know about the story of Modern Warfare 4, it seems we're neck deep in North Korea's invasion of South Korea by this point. The mission will follow a squad of South Korean marines (plus one embedded American) in an uphill offensive—we've got trenches, APCs, shotguns, and that thing where an NPC buddy has an elaborate mo-capped brawl right in front of you. In short: a Call of Duty mission, and perhaps a good one. Warzone will also make an appearance in a beta for the first time, but not until the second weekend. That's the one that's open for all, August 28 to September 1. The new Zodiac Resurgeance map will be playable, and I imagine we'll also learn the ways in which Warzone will be absorbing Modern Warfare 4's gameplay changes. (Image credit: Activision Blizzard) If you're not caught up, Infinity Ward's first CoD in four years appears to be more about refinements than anything else—clever solutions to things like muzzle flash, hipfire, and movement aimed at maintaining Modern Warfare's immersive qualities while not annoying serious players. I played a bit of multiplayer back in May against other journalists and had a good time, but next week's beta is a proper test drive. As for why Infinity Ward is double-stuffing the beta, it has not said, though one could intuit that the studio is extending an olive branch to fans disappointed by last year's pretty bad Black Ops 7 , and who might not see the urgency to buy another $70 CoD weeks before GTA6 arrives. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together
